author: TEDx Talks
description:
In Amir Hampel's talk, he reframes anxiety not as an internal defect, but as a byproduct of navigating unfamiliar "cultural languages", the unspoken norms and social cues that govern how we connect. Drawing from his research on mental health, he argues that the confusion many feel in social environments is often a sign of being in the process of learning a new cultural grammar rather than a personal failure. Amir encourages shifting from self-doubt to curiosity, emphasizing that confidence is built through active interaction rather than fixed traits. Ultimately, he reassures the audience that feeling like an outsider is simply a stage of learning, reminding us that "when you feel like something is wrong with you, it's likely just a language you're still mastering".

title: Anxious about socializing? You're not alone. | Amir Hampel | TEDxNYU Shanghai

description:
In this talk, Johnson Agbaje explores how the decisions we make internally often shape our actions long before the moment itself arrives. Through a relatable everyday metaphor and a personal experience that later led to a Police Public Bravery Award and Commissioner’s Commendation, he reflects on how hesitation, self-doubt, and pre-decided outcomes quietly influence the direction of our lives.

The talk challenges audiences to reconsider the moments they walk away from, not because they lack ability, but because they have already convinced themselves not to try. Jay Agbaje is the Students’ Association President at Arden University and an advocate for student voice, leadership, and meaningful action. Alongside his work in higher education and representation, he is also involved in entrepreneurial and innovation-focused projects centred around impact, sustainability, and future-focused thinking. title: Why We Decide Before We Even Try | Johnson Agbaje | TEDxArden University Manchester

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk examines neurodivergence, and the impact of language, labels, and societal expectations on those who think and experience the world differently. Blending lived experience with psychology and social insight, the talk challenges traditional ideas of “normal” and argues that autism and ADHD should be understood as natural forms of human variation rather than deficits or disorders. It also highlights the strengths often associated with neurodivergence, including creativity, empathy, innovation, and deep focus, while advocating for environments where all kinds of minds can thrive. Hannah Johnson Toyne is an English Language Lecturer and Neurodiversity Network Co-Chair at Arden University, as well as a psychology researcher and neurodiversity advocate. With a background in language teaching, linguistics, and psychology, her work explores the intersection of lived experience, education, and neurodiversity. title: Change the words, change the world | Hannah Johnson Toyne | TEDxArden University Manchester

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk shows how Higher Education can be reshaped by centring the lived experiences of disabled students. It highlights how traditional ideas about independence and resilience can create barriers and argues for learning environments that are designed with disabled students from the start. By treating students as partners and contributors, not as recipients of support, the talk shows how universities can build spaces that promote belonging, accessibility and shared ownership of learning. Lauren Hamilton is a Head of Department and an interdisciplinary researcher and academic with a background in Critical Disability Studies and Education. Lauren advocates  for an interdisciplinary approach to the study of disability discourse with an emphasis on achieving universal inclusion and acceptance. With over ten years’ experience in higher education, specialising in inclusive pedagogy, accessibility, and widening participation practice both Laurens personal and professional identity is roote
title: Reimagining HE Through Disabled Student Voices | Lauren Hamilton | TEDxArden University Manchester

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the key to transforming global education has been rooted in local communities all along? In this inspiring talk, Ezethu Sivuku explores how culture, identity, and indigenous knowledge can become powerful drivers of innovation in education. Drawing on his experience advancing technology and learning opportunities in South Africa, he demonstrates that the most impactful educational solutions don't come from replacing local perspectives—they come from building upon them. By embracing culture as a catalyst for creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving, Ezethu offers a compelling vision for an education system that prepares learners to thrive globally while remaining deeply connected to their communities. Ezethu Sivuku is a South African entrepreneur, innovator, and founder of NHUSTA, an emerging education technology venture dedicated to transforming how young people learn, grow, and unlock their potential. title: The Future Of Learning Is Local | Ezethu Sivuku | TEDxSummerstrand

Dr. Marc Triola is a Professor in the Department of Medicine at NYU Grossman School of Medicine. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Effective change management relies heavily on clear, early, and consistent communication, not just brilliant plans or technology. Authoritarian directives ("Because I said so") foster fear and resistance. Instead, leaders must communicate the "why" behind changes, focusing on human outcomes and purpose rather than corporate jargon.

Open, bilateral communication, including active listening and feedback, builds trust and ensures people feel included and understand the change. This approach, using frameworks like "What? So What? Now What?", helps integrate change smoothly. Ultimately, successful change management is about leading people effectively, ensuring they are supported and engaged throughout the transition. Jenn is an experienced Delivery professional specialising in Delivery and Transformations within Technical Delivery. title: Why communication is key to change management | Jenn Rigby | TEDxArden University Manchester

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores how many of us rule ourselves out of opportunities before the world has even had the chance to say yes or no. Through Kyle’s journey from dropping out of college and believing certain spaces were “for other people”, to finding confidence through university, AI leadership and community-building, he challenges the idea that we need to feel fully ready before we begin. As AI reshapes work, learning and opportunity, Kyle shows why the future belongs not to the most technical, but to those willing to start, adapt and build confidence in motion. Kyle Collins is a technology consultant at IBM Consulting, where he helps organisations explore AI, digital transformation and practical innovation. He is Chair of IBM UK&I’s Gen AI Society, leading initiatives that have supported thousands of professionals, students and clients to build confidence with emerging technology. A multi-award-winning professional, Kyle is passionate about making AI accessible, inclusive and useful for
title: The Future of AI Needs Translators | Kyle Collins | TEDxArden University Manchester

description: Immunotherapy is an incredible new cancer treatment that works by helping our own immune systems to fight cancer. The talk will cover the progress made with this treatment so far, the challenges that remain, and what cancer researchers are doing to overcome them. It reveals what this shift means for the future of cancer care, and why it could reshape how we treat cancer. Dr Ellie is a scientist working in cancer research. Her work mainly focuses on improving the diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer. In particular, she is interested in understanding why some people respond well to immunotherapy treatment, and why others do not. Initially trained as a mathematician, Ellie then sought to apply her computational skills to biomedical problems. After gaining a PhD from the University of Manchester, Ellie worked as a postdoctoral scientist in Stockholm, Sweden, where her work focused on identifying biomarkers for the early detection of Parkinson’s disease. title: Helping the immune system fight cancer | Dr Ellie Appleton-Pinto | TEDxArden University Manchester

description:
### Reading in a Digital World

In a world of endless notifications, short-form content, and constant digital distractions, reading is changing. But does living in a digital world mean we are losing our ability to read deeply?

This talk explores how technology is reshaping the way we read, think, and connect with ideas. It asks whether digital tools are replacing traditional reading—or giving us new ways to discover, understand, and experience literature.

**Reading in a Digital World** invites us to rethink our relationship with books and reminds us that, even in an age of screens, the power of a good story remains timeless.
